protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: Confirmed. An authenticated administrator can upload unsanitized SVG bytes with image/svg+xml, and the public /files middleware retrieves them with the configured API key then copies the body and Content-Type without Content-Disposition or CSP, allowing browser navigation to execute active SVG content.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: Primary BIC 0fdb790520a55b89f762babd97dc2765b6295411 is not the complete-mechanism BIC: its policy-protected Results.File calls pass fileDownloadName, which is used for Content-Disposition. PR #2216 member a80bdcf62f7c4e03763c3d35cc2ac535fef17148 is the smallest public commit that adds and activates RemoteFileProviderMiddleware for /files; it emits the stored Content-Type and bytes without propagating Content-Disposition, completing the public inline-execution path.
protocol_checks.immediate_parent_absence: Confirmed for corrected BIC. Parent d98d94aa05511d4510466c7c3ed212effade5b81 has neither RemoteFileProviderMiddleware nor a /files middleware mapping; a80bdcf62f7c4e03763c3d35cc2ac535fef17148 creates the middleware and activates it in Program.cs.
protocol_checks.squash_member_decomposition: Confirmed. Squash 9517ad5a48e986acb81c6c42ad9e2cf9e0c1df9a is the single-parent merge of PR #2216; the public PR member list identifies a80bdcf62f7c4e03763c3d35cc2ac535fef17148 as '#1939 add file download controller', and its patch is the atomic first write of the vulnerable public serving path.
protocol_checks.affected_release_membership: Confirmed by tag content. v0.0.1 contains the active /files middleware and unsanitized upload/serve path in its reinitialized main history; v0.0.2 through v0.0.5 contain squash 9517ad5a48e986acb81c6c42ad9e2cf9e0c1df9a and the same mechanism. The repository has no 1.2.3 tag.
protocol_checks.fixed_release_membership: No fixed release exists. The only repository tags are v0.0.1 through v0.0.5, all contain the vulnerable mechanism, and none contains sanitizer commit 81dad4805df593dae8c22184b5a0533685287198.
protocol_checks.direct_fix_or_verified_unpatched: Verified unpatched. GitHub reports PR #2407 open, draft, unmerged, head 81dad4805df593dae8c22184b5a0533685287198; that commit directly sanitizes SVG before fileStorageProvider.Upload, but it is not an ancestor of dev. GitHub and local origin/dev both resolve to c63d49cdbc1f4051d34bb71087d904c56e33951e, whose FileService still stores the raw stream and has no SanitizeSvg.
protocol_checks.bic_only_ai_attribution: Corrected BIC a80bdcf62f7c4e03763c3d35cc2ac535fef17148 is authored and committed by Amir Pournasserian <amir.pournasserian@live.com>; its commit object contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, agent, bot, Copilot, ChatGPT, or Claude marker. AI markers on the unmerged fix commit are irrelevant to BIC attribution, so the substantive verdict remains NOT_AI.

findings: The primary record identifies the wrong atomic introducer. Commit 0fdb790520a55b89f762babd97dc2765b6295411 first stores raw uploads, but its download is policy-protected and supplies fileDownloadName for Content-Disposition; it does not create the advisory's unauthenticated public inline-SVG sink.

PR #2216 member a80bdcf62f7c4e03763c3d35cc2ac535fef17148 first creates and activates the public /files proxy that drops Content-Disposition while forwarding executable SVG bytes and Content-Type. Its parent lacks that path, so this is the corrected atomic BIC.

Changing the BIC does not change the verdict: the corrected BIC has only human author/committer identity and no AI marker. The case remains a real, currently unpatched vulnerability with NOT_AI authorship.

corrected_fields.flaw_origin: The complete stored-XSS mechanism first appears in PR #2216 member a80bdcf62f7c4e03763c3d35cc2ac535fef17148 ('#1939 add file download controller', 2024-11-03). Earlier 0fdb790520a55b89f762babd97dc2765b6295411 introduced unsanitized persistence and a policy-protected Results.File download that supplies fileDownloadName, but not the public inline-serving sink. a80bdcf62f7c4e03763c3d35cc2ac535fef17148 creates RemoteFileProviderMiddleware, maps it to /files, fetches via the API client key, copies Content-Type and body, and omits Content-Disposition/CSP. Its immediate parent d98d94aa05511d4510466c7c3ed212effade5b81 lacks both the middleware file and mapping. The later squash 9517ad5a48e986acb81c6c42ad9e2cf9e0c1df9a lands that member on dev.
